items.question: Under what conditions must this teaching be kept secret?
premises: The teaching must be concealed
Concealment requires deliberate effort
Secrecy applies in the mortal world among the lowest people
items.inference: This teaching should be carefully hidden from unworthy people in the mortal world.
items.plain_english: It must be carefully concealed in the mortal world among the lowest of men.

items.question: To whom may this teaching legitimately be transmitted?
premises: The teaching may be given
The recipient should be previously accomplished
The recipient must be tested for one year
items.inference: Transmission is permitted only to a previously accomplished person tested for one year.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is already accomplished and has been tested for one year.

items.question: Which chapter concludes in the text emerged from Candradvīpa?
premises: The text is identified as emerged from Candradvīpa
The section is numbered fifth
The section is called a chapter
items.inference: This marks the end of the fifth chapter in the Candradvīpa recension.
items.plain_english: Thus ends the fifth chapter in the text that emerged from Candradvīpa.

items.question: What understanding has the speaker gained through the lord's grace?
premises: The speaker addresses the lord of Kaulas
Understanding arose by the lord's grace
The object understood is the determination of Kaula
items.inference: By the lord's grace, the speaker has come to know the Kaula doctrine.
items.plain_english: O Lord of the Kaulas, by your grace I have understood the determination of the Kaula teaching.

items.question: What is the declared identity and essential nature of the soul?
premises: The soul has been declared in the teaching
Its identity is questioned
Its essential nature is also questioned
items.inference: The inquiry seeks both who the soul is and what its true nature is.
items.plain_english: Who is that soul that has been declared, and what is the true nature of the soul?

items.question: Into what does the soul dissolve, and what full explanation is requested?
premises: The soul's place of dissolution is questioned
The speaker asks for a complete account
The request is directed to the teacher
items.inference: The teacher is asked to explain fully where the soul dissolves.
items.plain_english: And into what does it dissolve? Tell me all of that.

items.question: What supreme qualities define the true nature of that reality?
premises: That reality is described as supreme
It is partless and eternal
It is free from disease and stainless
items.inference: The reality in question is characterized as supreme, partless, eternal, and pure.
items.plain_english: He is supreme, partless, eternal, free from disease, and stainless.

items.question: How is the supreme soul identified in relation to haṃsa and individual power?
premises: The soul is described as supreme
That same soul is identified as haṃsa
It is also characterized as power and individual
items.inference: The supreme soul is identified as haṃsa, the individual endowed with power.
uncertainties: The exact doctrinal sense of śakti+pudgalaḥ is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: That soul is supreme; indeed, he is the haṃsa, the individual endowed with power.

items.question: Where is the breath-filled vital air said to be situated?
premises: The vital air is described as filled with breath
It is said to be situated
Its location is in all beings
items.inference: The breath-filled vital air abides in all living beings.
items.plain_english: The breath-filled vital air is situated in all living beings.

items.question: What identity is ascribed to the soul upon merely leaving the body?
premises: The condition is merely leaving the body
The subject is then designated
The designation is supreme Śiva
items.inference: Upon leaving the body, that soul is called supreme Śiva.
items.plain_english: As soon as he leaves the body, he is called the supreme Śiva.

items.question: How is this teaching transmitted and received according to tradition?
premises: The teaching is heard in the ear
The goddess is addressed as recipient
It has come down through traditional succession
items.inference: This teaching is received aurally through an unbroken traditional lineage.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, it is heard in the ear, having come down through the succession of tradition.

items.question: What is the effect of merely hearing this knowledge?
premises: The knowledge is received by hearing
Mere knowledge is emphasized
The fair-faced one is addressed
items.inference: Even merely hearing this knowledge has significance for the practitioner.
uncertainties: The specific result is completed in the following verse.
items.plain_english: O fair-faced one, by this mere knowledge that has been heard...

items.question: What disciplined practice over six months leads toward freedom from bondage?
premises: Practice is prescribed for six months
The practitioner is described as one who practices
The state aimed at is free from bondage
items.inference: One who practices for six months attains a state free from bondage.
uncertainties: The role of kāṣāyaṃ may be literal or symbolic.
items.plain_english: But whoever practices for six months, wearing the ochre robe, becomes free from bondage.

items.question: What benefits follow from the prescribed practice of the soul?
premises: The practitioner becomes freed from all diseases
The practitioner gains association with yogis
Union with yogis is achieved
items.inference: The practice results in freedom from disease and communion with yogis.
items.plain_english: Freed from all diseases, he attains union together with the yogis.

items.question: What teaching has now been fully communicated to Bhairavī?
premises: The speaker addresses Bhairavī
The subject communicated is the practice of the soul
The communication is declared complete
items.inference: The teaching on the practice of the soul has been told to Bhairavī.
items.plain_english: O Bhairavī, this practice of the soul has now been told to you.

items.question: What qualities qualify a recipient to receive this teaching?
premises: The teaching may be given
The recipient is endowed with all states
The recipient has a resolved mind
items.inference: This teaching should be given to a fully endowed and firmly resolved person.
uncertainties: The phrase sarva+bhāva+upapannasya is open to interpretive nuance.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is endowed with all states and has a firmly resolved mind.

items.question: To whom must the essential Kaula teaching originating from the yoginīs not be given?
premises: The Kaula essence is identified
Its origin is from the yoginīs
Transmission of this essence is prohibited
items.inference: The essential Kaula teaching originating from the yoginīs must not be given indiscriminately.
items.plain_english: The essential Kaula teaching, which originates from the yoginīs, must not be given.

items.question: What transformation of the speaker's body is claimed after receiving knowledge?
premises: The speaker refers to the present moment
The body is now described as pure
It was previously struck by the veil of ignorance
items.inference: The speaker claims that her body, once veiled by ignorance, is now pure.
items.plain_english: Today my body is pure, though it was once struck by the veil of ignorance.

items.question: What auspicious knowledge about overcoming time does the speaker now seek?
premises: The speaker expresses a present wish
The wish is to hear a teaching
The teaching concerns the deception of time
items.inference: The speaker now wishes to hear the auspicious means of overcoming time.
items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear the auspicious teaching on the deception of time.

items.question: What assurance is given about the destruction of death through this teaching?
premises: The teacher promises to explain
There is said to be no doubt
The explanation concerns how death is destroyed
items.inference: The teacher assures that death can be destroyed and will explain how.
items.plain_english: I will tell you without doubt how death is destroyed.

items.question: Why can even a wise person be afflicted despite contact with nectar's essence?
premises: There is contact with the tip of nectar
There is burning by the essence of juice
Even a wise person is affected
items.inference: Even the wise may suffer burning despite proximity to nectar's essence.
uncertainties: The physiological or yogic referent of amṛta+agraṃ is not explicit.
items.plain_english: Even a wise person may burn at the tip of nectar by the essence of its juice.

items.question: What yogic technique is prescribed to counteract the burning at the nectar point?
premises: The practice is located at the root of tongue and palate
The practitioner prepares the position
The practitioner should slowly drink the air
items.inference: The remedy is to slowly draw in the breath at the root of the tongue and palate.
items.plain_english: Placing oneself at the root of the tongue and palate, one should slowly drink the air.

items.question: What result follows from practicing this technique for one year?
premises: The practice is continued for one year
The condition is sustained practice
Old age and death are said to be destroyed
items.inference: Practicing this technique for one year destroys old age and death.
items.plain_english: When practiced for one year, old age and death are destroyed.

items.question: What protective power against poison results from this accomplished practice?
premises: The practitioner may be bitten by great serpents
Poison is the expected threat
Poison does not enter the body
items.inference: The accomplished practitioner becomes immune to poison even from great serpents.
items.plain_english: Even if bitten by great serpents, poison does not enter the body.
